sections.title: DSP updates
notes: PATCH /api/buses/<id> accepts a dsp wrapper and merges the supplied fields into the in-memory project while applying them to the engine. POST /api/buses/<id>/dsp accepts the DSP object directly and applies a temporary engine-only change. The method entries below specify their authentication, responses and errors.

A successful PATCH returns {"ok":true} and broadcasts doc_patch with op "buses_patched", containing all stored bus definitions and their DSP. HTTP response and WebSocket event ordering is not guaranteed. PATCH does not itself save the project file; POST /api/project/save writes the current document after a project path is set.

POST /api/buses does not apply DSP settings during bus creation; use PATCH afterward. Defaults in the field tables describe a fresh bus. Omitted update fields retain stored values. Unknown keys are ignored; null is not a reset operation. Type errors can return 400, and partial mutation has no transactional rollback guarantee.

examples.title: Change one compressor parameter, retaining its other values

sections.title: EQ bands: frequency, gain, Q, type, add and remove
notes: Slots are zero-based. To change band 2, send two empty objects then its patch. Empty objects retain existing slots. A shorter array leaves later bands unchanged; eq:[] clears nothing. Do not splice an interior band out of your cache and resend the shifted array.

Append at the current eq.length (maximum 32), or reuse an inactive interior slot with on:true. Extending across unused indices creates default enabled bands in the gaps; avoid this by using existing slots or appending exactly one.

Disable with on:false. The server trims all disabled slots at the array tail, so re-fetch or consume the next buses_patched before assigning another slot. Interior disabled slots remain. To clear every band, send on:false at every current slot.

Use type for new integrations. Serialized bands include shelf for compatibility: do not echo a stale shelf:false alongside type:"lowShelf" or type:"highShelf", because shelf is applied afterward and changes it back to bell. Send only the fields being edited, or remove shelf from a full read-modify-write payload.

Bell uses freq/gain/q; shelves use freq/gain/slope; lowCut/highCut/notch use freq/q and ignore gain. Separate HPF/LPF controls are independent of cut bands. eqEnabled bypasses the band array while retaining its settings.

sections.title: Separate high-pass and low-pass filters
notes: Each is a single biquad with freq and q. There is no on, type, gain, slope or selectable filter-order field for these two sections. EQ shelf slope is not a filter steepness control.

HPF processes above 20 Hz; LPF processes below 20000 Hz, with nonpositive values interpreted as their parked defaults. Bypass by setting HPF to 20 and LPF to 20000. eqEnabled does not bypass these filters.

The API stores their frequency as supplied rather than clamping it. Engine coefficient design clamps frequency to its sample-rate limits (upper limit 0.49 × sample rate), so a readback is a stored setting, not necessarily the effective corner frequency.

sections.title: Expander / gate
notes: The gate object is the downward expander/gate; there is no separate expander object. The detector is stereo-linked. Threshold, ratio and attenuation range set the expansion behavior.

Both dynEnabled and gate.on must be true. A ratio of 1 or range of 0 also makes the processor inactive. Attack opens the gate; release closes it. Read gate_gr_db from the bus mixer meter for actual reduction.

examples.title: Enable an expander/gate with explicit timing
Change threshold alone
Bypass the gate, keeping the compressor available

sections.title: Compressor / bus limiting
notes: Both dynEnabled and comp.on must be true. Ratio 1 with zero makeup bypasses processing; ratio 1 with nonzero makeup is still an active gain stage.

The detector is stereo-linked; compression uses a soft knee when knee >0. Attack increases attenuation and release recovers it. A high ratio is available, but this bus compressor has no lookahead and is separate from the master brick-wall limiter.

sections.title: Stereo image, bass mono and pan
notes: dsp.width.width controls the stereo image. Top-level bus.width is channel count (1 or 2); these are different controls. Stereo image processing is ignored for mono buses.
There is no width.on switch. Width 1 with bassMonoHz 20 is neutral; width 0 folds to mono. Bass-mono filtering attenuates low-frequency side content rather than imposing a sharp crossover.

Pan/balance is top-level bus.pan, not inside dsp. It clamps to -1..1. Preview mono-check overrides the preview-role bus image to mono without changing its stored DSP. dynEnabled and eqEnabled do not bypass stereo image processing.

sections.title: Section bypass
notes: There is no global DSP bypass field. eqEnabled controls EQ bands; dynEnabled controls gate and compressor. Separate filters and stereo width each use their neutral/parked values.

Bypass preserves the settings within the bypassed EQ or dynamics section. The separate filters and stereo image have no independent bypass switches: setting them to neutral values changes their stored parameters. Restoring an earlier full DSP object can overwrite concurrent edits.

sections.title: Temporary DSP updates
notes: The request body is the DSP object itself, without a dsp wrapper. This method changes the engine only: it does not update the stored project or broadcast buses_patched. GET continues to return stored DSP.

Each request merges against stored DSP, not against the preceding temporary adjustment. For example, sending an EQ change followed by only a compressor change restores EQ to its stored value. Every temporary request must include all desired uncommitted changes to retain them.

PATCH /api/buses/<id> with {"dsp": {...}} stores and applies the supplied changes. POST /api/buses/<id>/dsp with {} reapplies stored DSP to the engine. Serialized EQ shelf flags must agree with type or be omitted.

fields: Each part is written; filename from Content-Disposition, default upload.bin.

errors: Handler exception (JSON parsing, type conversion or operation failure); message varies.

endpoints.notes: Also requires normal Bearer auth when login is enabled; this query token is not authentication. 200 application/octet-stream with Content-Disposition attachment. Redeems token and deletes temporary archive. Invalid/expired token: 404.

endpoints.title: Read a framework static file
endpoints.notes: Crow registers this automatically at run(): serves sanitized relative names from static/ under the process working directory. It is not the public docs website and is not checked by LivePlay fsRoots. Missing files return framework 404; MIME type is based on extension. Example: GET /static/example.txt returns its contents only if that file exists. HEAD follows GET without a response body.

schemas.name: ProjectItem
schemas.description: Project item objects are preserved as JSON; the server does not enforce a complete item schema. Use the following current control fields. On PATCH, omitted fields retain their values. Defaults below describe runtime fallbacks, which can differ from defaults supplied by the desktop importer.
fields: audio or group are the playable item types; action is present in client types but has no general trigger implementation.
Zero-based playlist location; API by-index resolves tree order.
Nearest ancestor busId, then Master-role bus; applies to groups and audio.
Engine identity for an audio item; can change when reloading.
Path relative to project folder; prefer media/<filename>.
Host-specific absolute fallback; existing relative mediaPath takes precedence.
Client waveform cache: length integer, duration seconds, peaks number[], optional channelPeaks number[][]; not the REST Waveform shape.
1 is unity; client range 0..2; server maps <=0.0001 to -120 dB without enforcing the UI maximum.
End fade is max(stopFade, fadeOutDuration); also manual-stop fallback.
Loop overlap, capped at half trimmed duration.
Wait before next/goto; ignored with overlapping transitions.
Absolute file position that triggers next.
action: nothing/next/goto-item/goto-index/loop; targetUuid string or targetIndex integer[] as needed.
Audio action: nothing/play-next/play-item/play-index, with targetUuid/targetIndex. Group: play-first/play-all.
mode: no-ducking/stop-all/duck-others; duckLevel linear number, duckFadeIn/duckFadeOut seconds.
Each has timePoint seconds and action object; see CustomAction.

schemas.name: CustomAction
schemas.description: The sequencer processes timed actions on project audio items. HTTP actions are sent to clients for execution; the server does not issue an outbound HTTP request.
fields: url string, method GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, contentType form/json, optional body object. Desktop executes; server does not validate.

schemas.name: ProjectDocument
schemas.description: Full .liveplay-style document. GET adds engine annotations and server state; these response-only values are not a portable persistence contract. Inline documents should use items; the loader also accepts compatible engine-oriented files. Save through the API to apply persistence cleanup.
fields: Top-level playlist; nested children stay in groups.
slot integer (0..63), itemUuid string; server stores index [-1, slot].
Slot bindings: key string; ctrlKey/shiftKey/altKey booleans.
Persisted bus definitions; runtime fields absent.
Computed from the loaded/saved .liveplay location; removed on disk.
projectFilePath/mediaRoot strings; audioLoading bool; audioLoaded/audioTotal integers.
Read for seeding user preferences; not maintained as project preferences.

schemas.name: ProjectHeader
schemas.description: Returned by header/document/load. Does not include the playlist items or bus definitions. All listed header keys are emitted; load adds repair and optional migration fields.
fields: settings is ProjectSettings; other maps may be empty.
True when top-level items exist or a project file path is set.
Included by document/load when normalization reports changes.

schemas.name: ProjectLoad
schemas.description: ProjectHeader plus the following load fields.

schemas.name: ItemPage
schemas.description: Pagination is over top-level items only.
fields: Page with nested children and available cueId annotations.

schemas.name: ProjectSettings
schemas.description: Sparse accepted settings; invalid/unknown keys are dropped. All writable fields optional. Read responses also contain derived outputTargetLevels. Defaults below are runtime fallbacks or explicitly identified client defaults.
fields: Logical timecode output; empty/null disconnects it.
Disable master limiter for this project.
Automatic arming when no end behavior is set.
Accepted for compatible documents; normalized into bus/output configuration. Use buses and ltcOutput for new integrations.

schemas.name: Bus
schemas.description: GET includes all runtime fields below. PATCH accepts name/color/order/width/gainDb/mute/pan/dsp/output/sends plus role acquisition. Creation accepts only the fields listed on POST /api/buses.
fields: Clamped -1..1. Mono: constant-power pan. Stereo: balance.
To acquire a role send true; false is refused. One role each, never both on one bus. Role holders need output.type=output.
Replaces entire list; [] clears. Preview cannot send or be a destination. Combined output/send graph must be acyclic.
Live listen/mono state and whether output reaches hardware.
Hardware-bound master pair; house 0/1, Preview highest pair.
Engine strip ID; may be empty during rebuild.
Audio items whose bus resolves here, including inherited assignments.

schemas.name: BusOutput
schemas.description: Routing types are explicitly serialized. The supported compatibility value master (and unrecognized types) resolves to the current Master-role bus. Prefer explicit types for new integrations.
fields: Bus id for bus; logical output or present device name for output; ignored/cleared for none.

schemas.name: BusSend
schemas.description: Auxiliary copy of a bus signal. No send is a separate hardware assignment.
fields: pre: after processing, before fader/mute; all other strings read as post.

schemas.name: BusDsp
schemas.description: Complete stored bus DSP. Every field is emitted on reads; fields are optional in partial updates. Defaults describe a fresh bus. Omitted fields retain stored values, not defaults. EQ merges by slot (0..31); nested processor objects merge by field. Read it in a bus response; update it with the bus PATCH or live DSP POST methods.
fields: Enables the EQ band array only; does not bypass the separate HPF/LPF.
Enables gate and compressor together; does not bypass stereo width.
Stored without a frequency clamp. Active above 20; <=0 uses 20 internally. Park at 20 to bypass.
Clamped to 0.1..40. Resonance of the separate high-pass biquad.
Stored without a frequency clamp. Active when >0 and <20000; <=0 uses 20000 internally. Park at 20000 to bypass.
Clamped to 0.1..40. Resonance of the separate low-pass biquad.
Index-wise merge, maximum 32 slots (0..31). Initial (freq Hz, q): (100,0.7), (500,1), (2500,1), (10000,0.7). Missing trailing entries remain. [] does not clear bands.
False disables the slot; trailing disabled slots are removed. Interior slots keep their indices. Not a separate stable band ID.
Clamped to 10..24000. Existing slots retain their frequency when omitted. Engine filter design also clamps to its sample-rate limits.
Clamped to -24..24. Used by bell/shelves; cuts and notch ignore gain. Flat bell/shelf is a no-op.
Clamped to 0.1..40. Used by bell, lowCut, highCut and notch. Shelves use slope instead.
Case-sensitive: bell, lowShelf, highShelf, lowCut, highCut, notch. Unknown string retains the existing type. lowCut = high-pass; highCut = low-pass.
Clamped to 0.1..2. Shelf shape parameter, not dB/octave; 1 is the non-peaking steep shelf shape. Ignored by other types.
Compatibility input applied AFTER type. false turns a shelf into bell; true promotes non-shelves only at slot 0 (lowShelf) or 3 (highShelf). Omit this field when editing type.
Individual expander/gate switch; also requires dynEnabled, ratio >1 and range <0 to process.
Clamped to -80..0. Level below which downward expansion applies.
Clamped to 1..20. 1 is a no-op. Higher ratios produce stronger gating.
Clamped to -80..0. Maximum attenuation, expressed as a negative value. 0 is a no-op.
Clamped to 0..1000. Hold time before closing.
Individual compressor switch; also requires dynEnabled. Ratio 1 and makeup 0 is a no-op.
Clamped to 1..60. Ratio 1 with nonzero makeup still processes.
Clamped to -12..24. Output makeup gain; excluded from the reported gain-reduction value.
Clamped to 0.1..300. Time for gain reduction to increase.
Clamped to 0..24. Soft-knee width; 0 is a hard knee.
Clamped to 5..5000. Time for gain to recover.
Clamped to 0..2: 0 mono, 1 unchanged image, 2 wider. Stereo buses only. This differs from top-level bus.width, the channel count.
Clamped to 20..500. High-pass cutoff on the side signal to narrow low frequencies. Park at 20 to bypass bass-mono filtering.
Clamped to 0.1..4. Resonance of the side-signal high-pass.

schemas.name: OutputMap
schemas.description: Maps portable output names to host hardware. The channels array maps bus lanes in order. Unmapped Main Out resolves to the default device; unmapped Preview Out is silent. Other unmapped names bind only if a matching device is present.
fields: Each: name string; channels array of {device:string, hwChannel:integer}. Hardware channels are zero-based; nonempty device required.

schemas.name: UserPrefs

Nonempty, at most 4096 bytes; REST origin header and WS Origin gate.

schemas.name: MeterSample
schemas.description: All meter sample keys are emitted. dB fields use -120 as the silence floor. peak/rms are dBFS; true_peak uses dBTP. kw_ms values are linear K-weighted mean-square energy, not dB.

Raw sample maximum since the server consumed the previous meter interval.
True-peak equivalents; analysis may be gated off if no active meter mode needs it.
K-weighted energy, approximately 400 ms and 3 s windows. Loudness for summed channels: -0.691 + 10*log10(sum energy); guard zero.

events.notes: Fetch GET /api/buses on initial connection, after reconnect/project changes and when bus topology changes to obtain mixerId mappings. playback_snapshot carries compact bus state without dsp, and there is no initial full-DSP WebSocket snapshot or replay.

Empty arrays are valid idle state. See Meters and MeterSample for populated objects. In meters.mixer_channels, match mixer_id to the Bus.mixerId obtained over HTTP. gate_gr_db and comp_gr_db are non-positive dB values (0 = no reduction), reporting deepest reduction since the last meter tick. dyn_in_db/dyn_out_db are pre-fader dynamics input/output peak levels in dBFS. correlation reports stereo agreement (+1 aligned, 0 uncorrelated, negative cancellation). Meters do not carry the DSP parameter settings.
